name: comp-479
title: Sortable Columns Table
description: A dark account table with more columns than fit, showing name, email, country flag and city, status and balance. Clicking a header sorts the rows and drags a thin divider beside it to widen or narrow the column.
use: A wide record table needs click-to-sort headers and draggable column widths without adopting a full grid product.
avoid: Ten columns overflow a narrow screen and there is no responsive layout, so the right side clips or needs a scroll box.
a11y: Headers are focusable, sort on Enter or Space and set aria-sort, but the drag resize handles carry no label. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Small grey header labels sit on a slightly lighter band above five rows. Names are bold, locations start with a flag emoji, emails are cut short with an ellipsis, and balances line up at the right. Thin vertical dividers mark the column edges.
behaves: Clicking a header sorts by that column and swaps in an up or down chevron; a second click reverses it. Dragging the divider on a header's right edge widens the column, double-clicking it restores the original width.
customise: Columns, sort defaults and the fetch URL are fixed in the file; adding fields, changing widths or the row limit is a source edit.
weight: moderate: A table library sorts and resizes ten columns over five remote rows, with no animation loop.
demo: Five employees (Alex Thompson, Sarah Chen, James Wilson, Maria Garcia, Lars Nielsen) with flags, emails and balances.
issues: Frames 2-6 clip the right Balance column; only frame 1 shows every column.
Every email is truncated to an ellipsis, hiding which address it is.
polishWhy: Sort arrows and resize grips work well, but clipped columns and chopped emails look cramped.
